findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hardcoded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables. These are readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunction/describe permissions and are also committed to version control, making them compromised credentials that should be revoked and rotated.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is deprecated and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the function exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption configuration for environment variables
findings.description: No KMS customer-managed key is specified for encrypting the Lambda environment variables, so sensitive values (including the hardcoded credentials) rely on the default AWS-managed key rather than an auditable, access-controlled customer-managed key.
